## Declared assumptions and kT's decisions

- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** kT declares AOI-2226 refractive-index matching and independently switchable clear/glare/dark plus visible/NIR modulation. NOT demonstrated at full scale. Zero numeric optical/IR cooling performance credited; worst Venus solar aperture heat explicitly included. Transparent dome and AOI thermal expansion/differential heat flux remain OPEN. Decision: Zero quantified thermal attenuation or dynamic optical performance credited. Worst-case glazing heat counted.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-25.** Torch heat package (kT, 2026-10-25): each pellet is wrapped in a shell of remass that soaks up the burn and leaves as exhaust. The shell must let no more than ~358 ppm of the burn's energy escape as light, counting its own glow (the reactor face's 10 MW/m2 limit); the design value is 180 ppm. With the model's other assumptions (torch/torch_heat_inputs.json: light 40% of fusion energy; He3-rich, spin-polarised fuel with 0.76% neutrons, 85% absorbed by the shell; plume contact 1e-4 of charged energy; coil shield transmission 1e-3), 1.40 GW reaches hot structure and 0.48 MW the magnet coils at 12.6 TW of fusion. These are assumptions, not results. Replaces v0.5.1's 387 MW (34 ppm) torch-leak gap. Decision: v0.5.2 torch heat package (kT chose the package and 1,750 K fins on 2026-10-25 and accepted this wording the same day): the remass shell lets no more than ~360 ppm of the burn's energy escape as light, counting its own glow; design value 180 ppm; with the heat model's other assumptions 1.40 GW reaches hot structure and 0.48 MW the magnet coils.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-25.** Hot fins run for life at 1750 K. Lithium heat pipes have run in lab tests to ~1,500 K and briefly ~1,800 K; years at 1750 K with burn cycling and neutron exposure is an engineering extrapolation (a technology milestone), not new physics. Fallback: 1,500 K fins, ~49 m span, ~30 t, still inside the reserve. Decision: kT: "Let's go 1750." Hot fins at 1,750 K, recorded as an engineering extrapolation (technology milestone), with 1,500 K fins as the fallback.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** TWO D-He3 house reactors each 50MW net, 10% minimum on line, 40kW/kg net and 75% direct conversion; 2226 engineering declarations, not tested physical hardware. One surviving unit supports known Metric HARD cryo 34.8MW at 1300K plus separately declared, explicitly NON-CANON 5MW field/control, E1 0.98×0.96 PMAD losses, and ordinary loads. Relational plant is consumer ONLY, Metric bank never a source. Environmental correction power remains OPEN. Decision: kT ACCEPTS dedicated TWIN D-He3 house reactors: 2×50MW net with declared 40kW/kg and 10% minimum each, 75% direct conversion. Relational plant is a consumer ONLY and Metric bank is not a source. The 900K canon cryo card scales to existing 1300K design; EXTRA Metric field/control electrical loads 1/2/3/5MW by mode are declared NON-CANON engineering screening, not proof of environmental correction. Reactor failure fallback staged. No whole-ship certification on new hash.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** At worst-case sunlight, the open crown adds ~100 kW of solar heating to habitat. In heat-pump-failed or cold-running passive backup the 16 Strata gores MUST CLOSE; clear/glare/dark AOI states may not be credited as heat rejection or solar exclusion. Solar absorption/IR-band partition and AOI switching performance are not physically qualified. Decision: Model-derived operating restriction: active open-crown worst Venus sun creates ~100kW load; heat pump failed requires closure. Physical controls remain unqualified.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-31.** Cold running (rev 7, F5 provisional item F5-TE-01): the tunable flanks drop from emissivity 0.85 to 0.1, so at the same skin temperature they radiate 12% as much. Heat is held, not removed: habitat heat 58.1 kW (x1.25), plus plant standby 10.0 kW and cryo standby 10.0 kW, less 7.1 kW still leaking through 177 m2 of low-e skin at 290 K warms the 50 t of protected water by 15 K in about 11.7 h (ideal no-standby ceiling 17.1 h). House reactors OFF; battery inefficiency 3.5 kW included. ENGINEERING_ASSUMPTION (screening placeholders 10+10 kW, NOT sourced or qualified); editable, replace with measured/engineering budget. Then the ship must open the strakes or switch the flanks back to normal. Detailed load-cycle variation, cryo plant duty, tank thermal coupling, and reserve storage remain open. The metallic look in the viewer is a proposed optical property. Decision: kT 2026-11-01: both reactors OFF in quiet/cold running; flywheel powers ~65kW essentials until thermal-buffer bound, not sub-10% reactor idle. Recalculate passive leak, flywheel discharge heat and existing 50t×15K buffer. No 2226 material/thermal coupling proof.

- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** Full faceted nose 1.2m ahead of old bow and gore hinges at 50deg break; actual retaining loads, impact, thermal cycling, 5g attachment paths and shutter transition mechanics UNSHOWN. - **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** Two 0.15t pressure hatches normally OPEN aft of L1/L2 ladder plane x=3m; L2-to-L1 (-x) pressure outflow passively pushes each leaf toward an L2-side seat, differential pressure reinforces closure. No sensor/power/actuation needed; seal proof, hinge moments, reverse-flow isolation and 4g crew passage NOT demonstrated. It is NOT new evidence of actuation, hinge torque, reverse-flow isolation or leak-tightness.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Berth viewports (v0.5.7): 10 x 0.5 m viewports keep the berth screen because acrylic plugs carry at least the g/cm2 they replace (armour 27.14 vs 27.0, ring 8.26 vs 8.0), so the ray screen, which treats the hull as continuous, is unchanged. Rev 3: the same plug kit is in every opening below the crown, including the L2 viewport band, and continues through the storm-shelter jacket (17 cm more acrylic for the 20 cm of water). Not yet shown: the dose. Acrylic is ~8% hydrogen by mass against water's 11%, so per g/cm2 it may stop cosmic-ray secondaries slightly less well; a transport check may ask for a thicker plug. Encapsulated for fire. Decision: Every opening below the crown carries an acrylic shield plug and insert with at least the g/cm2 they replace (armour 27, berth ring 8, shelter jacket 20), so berths and shelter keep their screens with the shutters open; the dose is accepted as a provision until a transport check (OLTARIS) is run; plugs are encapsulated and counted as fire load.

- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** kT adopted deeper pair: TWO independent full-pressure ~7m transparent ceramic domes, each 28mm nominal, primary apex X=-0.30m, backup X=-0.42m, at unchanged rim. Meridional shape X(r)=3.043118-3.343118*sqrt(1-(r/4.3)^2), 0<=r<=3.50. Ideal apex thin-shell stress 10.00MPa vs 15.56MPa prior; not real pressure test. - **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** AOI-2226 ~3.023m3 (~3t) gel between two separately sealed pressure domes, gap min normal 5.973cm with backup axial offset ~12cm. Neither pressure-bearing nor a pressure seal. Each independent dome MUST withstand full 101.3kPa after other's failure while optogel is present, WITHOUT shock, fracture, crack bridging or fast pressure-pulse coupling. The research has NO measured high-rate response or independent-shell survival test; do not credit impact damping. Rim slip/contact interfaces and >=56L illustrative thermal-expansion compliance still require engineering. Decision: kT accepts the REQUIREMENT that either dome survive full differential and the other's failure without destructive coupling through AOI. This is an accepted declaration, NOT evidence that this behaviour has been physically demonstrated.

- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-31.** Metric node faces (rev 7, kT 2026-10-26; Sol: AGREE, placement HOLD): 208 visible flush or recessed faces, 13 rings x 16 at 22.5 deg (rev 5 longeron-study layout). 76 are clear; the rest are flagged: 16 faces dust flow bow first, 12 on bay door, 80 on torch chain, 1 overlaps camera, 2 overlaps hold door, 1 overlaps window, 20 under stowed strake. - **ACCEPTED.** Storm shelter life support: 72 h for 10 people from the life-support room on the same deck (design provision, not computed). Decision: 72 h of life support for 10 people in the storm shelter, from the life-support room on the same deck, recorded as a design provision to be sized in detail later.
- **ACCEPTED.** Galactic cosmic rays: at 2026 free-space rates (1.8 mSv/day, ~657 mSv/yr) a crew member reaches NASA's 600 mSv career limit after ~333 days in deep space. Hull shielding barely changes this. Long careers aboard rely on canon's off-Earth MED-MOD-RADIATION milestone and crew time-in-space rules; this is a canon question, not something the hull can close. Decision: crew protection from galactic cosmic rays relies on canon's off-Earth MED-MOD-RADIATION milestone plus crew time-in-space limits.
- **ACCEPTED.** Torch neutrons and gammas: the shadow shield must attenuate the torch's neutron and gamma output so the dose rate inside the habitat during burns stays within crew limits. The v0.5.2 heat model puts neutrons at ~0.76% of the burn's energy with 85% absorbed by the remass shell; the dose itself is not computed here, only the shadow geometry is checked. Decision: covered by the same declared gap: the torch and shadow shield keep neutron and gamma dose in the habitat within crew limits during burns; the shadow geometry is checked (G6).
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** Protected 50t water draw order: service reservoir FIRST (24.750t); the L3 berth ring and extended-wall tanks (8.534t), aft service-wall shield return (0.229t) and storm shelter jacket (16.483t) LAST and REFILLED FIRST. Do not infer 40g/cm2 shielding after critical water is drawn: repeat G6. Protected water remains reserved from routine propulsion. This declares withdrawal/refill priorities; no pump plumbing or autonomous draw implementation is qualified. Decision: Operating water-management doctrine only, not an implemented water-pump controller. Normal protected consumption draws service tank first (24.75t at S5). Emergency-only after service exhaustion may consume other protected stores; maintain armour/berth and storm shielding by drawing L3 water ring/extended wall, 0.229t service return, and shelter jacket last. Refill shield-critical water before general service tank. Beyond service-tank withdrawal, prior G6 minimum is not guaranteed without a new ray screen. 50t protected inventory not changed.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** Crown uses Whipple-like stand-off, not physically impact-qualified: 37 removable 10mm ceramic bumper tiles, vacuum gap that varies approximately 0.39–1.16m axially to backup shell on the adopted deeper dome, then two independent full-pressure ceramic domes. No hypervelocity shielding strength claimed; AOI shielding credit zero. Crown-open speed and bow/flow-angle controls remain visibly UNQUALIFIED. Governing doctrine still low speed OR bow away from dust flow; closed for torch, radiation and Metric. Actual safe numeric thresholds and sensor/failure logic OPEN. Decision: Low-speed OR bow-away-from-dust-flow; gores closed for torch, radiation/particle risk and Metric. Speed/angle thresholds stay null/UNQUALIFIED, not invented or safety-certified. 10mm bumper pane, vacuum standoff, twin dome concept does NOT certify hypervelocity resistance.

Scene seat length 1.58m <2.10m source crew envelope; 2D seat/ladder/walkways and bare dome clearances NOT physical 3D access or 4g qualification. Crown sightlines are optimistic upper bounds only. This is not occupant-swept collision testing. Optional terrace chamfer NOT BUILT. Decision: kT accepts I4 3D suited-body fit and egress as DECLARED for conventional Wayfarer lab qualification. Items with a ledger line are located inside it (sensor turrets in mission systems, RF arrays, laser terminals and aft trackers in the avionics racks, forward trackers in the bow sensor ring, service ports in the service arm, vents in life support, the docking target in the collar): 1.85 t, no new mass. - **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Torch thrust-vector control: the magnetic nozzle steers the thrust line by up to 1.0 deg (asymmetric coil current). Needed: trim plus an assumed 0.5 deg thrust error (0.842 deg). The error is an engineering assumption, not a measured disturbance history; the authority is not a qualified nozzle capability. Decision: Declare 1 deg of torch thrust-vector authority (decision 2), on the assumed 0.5 deg thrust error.

Decision: kT accepts axial RCS plume clearance as DECLARED, not a new physical plume impingement calculation. Original 10° canted one-nozzle-per-cluster assumption remains.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** Long torch burns split into segments of at most 165 min ([V2 6113]) with 15 min coasts (engineering assumption; in free space the coasts change elapsed time, not delta-v). Decision: kT accepts segmented burn doctrine as DECLARED: ≤165min torch burn segments with ≥15min coasts. Coasts add elapsed time, not free-space delta-v. This is not Metric travel qualification.

- Crew doctrine (v0.5.6): sustained thrust capped at 4 g with people aboard (NASA OCHMO: +Gx 4 g tolerable up to at least 60 min); 5 g stays the structural rating, for emergencies. The cap changes burn times, not delta-v.

- Target 370 m3 (45 per crew, 25 per guest): reached 88%. A sixth deck (+2.6 m of habitat) would reach the target.
- Net habitable volume by deck: L1 53 m3, L2 81 m3, L3 77 m3, L4 57 m3, L5 57 m3
- Windows: the crown dome over L1 (25 m2), a panoramic viewport band round L2 (19.4 m2, 1.6 m tall in the lounge), 12 round viewports (4 shoulder on L1; L4 medical 2, storm shelter 2; L5 suits 1, workshop 2, vestibule 1) and 10 berth viewports (0.5 m) on L3. With every shutter open about 2.59 kW radiates through the low-e glazing; shutters close for night. The canon candidate suggests 10-16 windows; amendment v2.4f proposes more (kT's call). Below the crown every window has four panes, a dust shutter, a 12 deg armour splay and an acrylic shield plug
- Casualties move at 0 g (coast on the captain's order); under thrust they are treated in their couch or berth.
- Decks are perpendicular to the thrust axis; under thrust, aft is down. Above ~1.5 g everyone rides in a couch.
- Cabins by occupancy (v0.5.3, Sol's candidate): Captain's cabin 1 (15.6 m3 each), Crew cabin A 2 (7.8 m3 each), Guest cabin 4 (5.9 m3 each), Crew cabin B 3 (7.8 m3 each); 10 berths in 4 cabins. Private cabins removed by kT on 2026-10-25 (basis change, Sol to agree).
